labels.name: performance
labels.description: Slow or uses too much memory

issues.title: YAML anchors and aliases are expanded on format
issues.body:
Formatting a YAML file with `&default` anchors writes the expanded values and removes the anchors.

Fixed in 2.2.0.
issues.author: mkowalski

issues.title: Glob matching is slow with many ignore patterns
issues.body:
With 200+ entries in `.tidyignore`, startup takes 3 seconds on 2.1.x. Each pattern is compiled again for every file.

Fixed in 2.2.1 by caching compiled patterns.
issues.author: jtanaka

issues.title: Config file not found when run from a subdirectory
issues.body:
Running `tidy` in `packages/api` does not pick up `tidy.config.json` in the repository root. Expected it to search parent directories.

Fixed in 2.3.0.
issues.author: priya-s

issues.title: Crash on empty config file
issues.body:
**Version:** 2.4.0, Node 22.3, macOS 15

**Steps**
1. `touch tidy.config.json` (file is 0 bytes)
2. `tidy .`

**Result**
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rules')
    at loadConfig (dist/config.js:41:23)
    at main (dist/cli.js:12:18)
```

**Expected**
Either treat an empty file as `{}` or print a readable error. Deleting the file works around it.
issues.author: dlopez

issues.title: tidy --write leaves files empty when the disk is full
issues.body:
We run `tidy --write` in a nightly job. Last night the build volume filled up while it was running and 312 source files were left at 0 bytes. The originals are gone; we restored from git, but two engineers lost uncommitted work.

Looking at `dist/write.js`, the file is opened with the `w` flag (which truncates it) and the formatted text is written afterwards. If the write fails, nothing is restored. Writing to a temporary file and renaming it over the original would avoid this.

Version 2.4.0, Linux, ext4. Reproducible with a small tmpfs: fill it, run `tidy --write`, files are truncated.
issues.author: ops-hannah

issues.title: TypeError reading 'rules' when tidy.config.json is 0 bytes
issues.body:
Our scaffolding tool creates an empty `tidy.config.json` and fills it in later. If tidy runs in between, it dies with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rules')
    at loadConfig (dist/config.js:41:23)
```

tidycli 2.4.0 on Ubuntu 24.04. An empty config should not crash the tool.

issues.title: Add a --check flag for CI
issues.body:
In CI we want to fail the build when files are not formatted, without changing them. Today the only option is `tidy --write` followed by `git diff --exit-code`, which is slow and awkward.

Proposal: `tidy --check` lists the files that would change and exits with code 1 if there are any, 0 otherwise. Prettier and gofmt have the same.

issues.title: --output accepts ../ paths from a shared config and overwrites files outside the project
issues.body:
A config pulled in with `extends` can set `output` to a path such as `../../.ssh/authorized_keys`. tidy then writes the formatted result there without any check.

Because `extends` accepts an npm package name, a malicious or compromised shared config can overwrite any file the user can write to, simply by the user running `tidy --write`.

Reproduced on 2.4.0:
```json
{ "extends": "./shared.json" }
```
with `shared.json` containing `{ "output": "../../outside.txt" }`. `outside.txt` is created two levels above the project.

Suggested fix: resolve `output` and refuse anything outside the project root unless `--allow-outside-root` is passed.
issues.author: sec-ren

issues.title: 2.4.0 is about 10x slower than 2.3.2 on a large monorepo
issues.body:
Same repository (about 5,200 files), same machine:

| version | time |
|---|---|
| 2.3.2 | 3.9s |
| 2.4.0 | 41s |

A CPU profile shows most of the time in `resolveConfig`, which now seems to run once per file instead of once per directory. Pinning 2.3.2 works for now, but we cannot take the 2.4 fixes.

Node 22.3, Linux.
